newsitem.title: USA: NYC Council agrees to delay date for new budget.
newsitem.headline: NYC Council agrees to delay date for new budget.

text.p: The New York City Council on Monday said it approved Mayor Rudolph Giuliani's request to delay when it has to adopt a new fiscal budget by five days to give Giuliani more time to assess tax collections.
The deadline was shifted to June 10, and the rest of the process also was delayed.
The following table breaks down the delays, which council officials said are not unusual for New York City's budget process.
--Mayor submits an executive budget, budget message and 10-year capital strategy on May 8, instead of April 26.
--Borough presidents recommendations, due on May 19, instead of May 6.
--Independent Budget Office submits report on mayor's budget on May 27, instead of May 15.
--Council holds hearings, which now must finish by May 30, instead of by May 25.
--If an expense budget is not adopted, a current, modified budget and existing rates are extended on June 10, not June 5.
--If capital budget not adopted, unutilized part of all prior capital appropriations deemed re-appropropriated, modified budget and existing tax rates extended on June 10, not June 5.
--Mayoral veto, due four days after council acts on budget, one day less than in the city charter, and council override vote due 10 days later, unchanged.
-Mayor's revenue estimate due June 6, instead of June 5. Giuliani had asked for a delay until June 10.
--Alernative revenue estimates, due June 3, instead of May 15.
--Fixing of tax rates, due June 10, instead of June 5.
